acceptanceCriteria: Every containment decision site is inventoried; each accepts ANCESTOR, or EQUIVALENT <sha> when `git cherry <source> <commit>` (patch-id) finds an equivalent commit, recording the equivalent SHA so provenance stays auditable; strict-ancestry-only sites that must stay strict are named with the reason.

A read-only query `source contains <rev> <commit...>` reports per commit ANCESTOR | EQUIVALENT <sha> | ABSENT, and distinguishes ABSENT-patch-differs (a commit with the same subject/change-id exists but its patch differs, e.g. conflict-resolved rebase) from plainly absent; it writes nothing.
Bounded: the patch-id scan has a named commit/byte bound; exceeding it yields UNKNOWN, never ABSENT or EQUIVALENT.
Spec requirements with tests for rebase, cherry-pick, conflict-resolved rebase, merge-only and bound-exceeded cases; Closes #1186.
body: GitHub #1186. Source-containment checks (pool --source provenance, prerequisite/commit-integrated checks, release candidates) use strict merge-base --is-ancestor. A rebased or cherry-picked commit whose content is present is reported missing; workers then repeatedly request fenced repins to older sources, burning sessions on already-deployed code.
title: Source containment: accept patch-equivalent (rebased/cherry-picked) commits as CONTAINED_EQUIVALENT and add read-only `source contains` (#1186)
